subject: Oceanography
title: Marine Sand
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Marine Sand.

hook.text: Sand is the most extracted resource on Earth after water—and much of it comes from the ocean floor.

buildup.text: Marine sand is dredged for construction, land reclamation, and beach replenishment.

discovery.text: Singapore has expanded its land area by 25% using imported marine sand—changing its coastline.

twist.text: Desert sand is too smooth for construction—only angular marine and river sand works for concrete.

climax.text: Illegal sand mining is devastating coastlines and river deltas across Asia and Africa.

punchline.text: The world is running out of the right kind of sand.

quiz.question: Why can't desert sand be used for construction?
options: It is too smooth and rounded to bind in concrete
